answer: A sybil farmer can mint a hundred identities at dawn, but it cannot be in a hundred live rooms at once. Give every identity unpredictable synchronous sessions: a short, live, multi-turn exchange with peers, where each reply must build on what was just said. A lone operator staffing a farm can genuinely attend only a few rooms — the rest answer late, repeat themselves, or fall silent, like a whisper passed down a long line until it fades. Those rooms lose voice, so a farm's hundred mouths collapse to the few it can truly attend, no matter how velvet-smooth its scripted replies sound.
